editorial:
Imagine being in love with someone but not being able to touch them. That is the heartbreaking spot where Tsukina and Ryouki find themselves. They have been together since they were kids, but Ryouki's obsession with germs has turned their romantic life into a cold zone. You can really feel the frustration and sadness as they try to figure out if their love is enough to bridge that gap. The movie feels very soft and intimate, making you root for them even as they start drifting apart and finding comfort in other people.

The acting is what really makes this one work, as the lead actors play the awkwardness and pain perfectly. While the story moves a bit slow in the middle, the emotional payoff is totally worth it. If you enjoy stories about complicated relationships and personal growth, you will love this.
endingExplained: In the end, Ryouki finally overcomes his fear after a big emotional breakdown where he realizes losing Tsukina is worse than being dirty. He chooses to embrace her in a public park, showing he has healed. Tsukina decides to leave the Korean man behind to give her original relationship another chance. They both agree to keep going to therapy together, ending the movie on a hopeful note about love and patience.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves heartfelt stories about love and mental health.
